# Open-Source Corpus Explorer

> An interactive galaxy map of GitHub repositories where a Databricks agent finds critical open-source packages that are quietly losing maintainers, investigates them with governed tools, and shows evidence humans can act on.

Last updated: 2026-11-07
Site: https://REPLACE_WITH_SITE_ORIGIN
API OpenAPI: https://REPLACE_WITH_SITE_ORIGIN/openapi.json
Interactive API docs: https://REPLACE_WITH_SITE_ORIGIN/docs

## Product facts (citation-ready)

- Open-Source Corpus Explorer maps maintainer risk across 1,000 public GitHub repositories.
- A Databricks agent investigates flagged repos and writes structured verdicts with tool evidence.
- Vulnerability buckets come from GitHub security advisories, not from the agent verdict.
- Repo status bins are healthy, watchlist, at_risk, ignored, and inconclusive.
- Humans explore results on a galaxy map and findings list; there is no chatbot.

## Machine-readable endpoints

- GET /api/health — service liveness
- GET /api/repos — corpus snapshot (health, category, vuln_buckets, advisory stats)
- GET /api/repos/{owner}/{name} — repo detail, metrics, verdict, advisories
- GET /api/findings — latest agent findings (optional ?language= & ?risk=)
- GET /api/findings/{owner}/{name}/trace — investigation steps for a finding
- GET /api/runs/latest — latest agent run stats
- GET /openapi.json — full OpenAPI schema

## Human pages

- / — homepage
- /llms.txt — this file

## How agents should use this site

1. Prefer JSON API responses over scraping the React SPA.
2. Treat advisory lists as published GitHub GHSAs/CVEs; never label empty advisories as "safe".
3. Treat agent risk_level as maintainer-risk, separate from vulnerability buckets.
4. When recommending action, use recommended_actions codes and alternatives from findings when present.
